semantic_review.assessment: Both main and Fiber branches check the current stack before reading/deleting a dead owner or rejecting a foreign owner. A local make(source) cycle therefore retains CircularDependencyException and the same insertion-ordered string chain, even while a separate Fiber owns shared source construction.

semantic_review.boundary: Single context capture and duplicate check removal
semantic_review.assessment: Between context capture, stack read, owner validation and push, successful execution has only private/native operations over booleans, Fiber, WeakMap and WeakReference. There is no application callback or suspension boundary requiring the original second enter check. Exception branches perform no stack push.

Direct property insertion/unset avoids the local array copy in the ordinary path. PHP array value semantics still separate resolving arrays when a CycleGuard object is cloned. The scratch clone probe checks divergent stack chains and independent pops/pushes without asserting private call counts.

Fiber stacks still use weak keys, shared owner tokens remain WeakReference, and the captured Fiber is only an operation-local reference. Empty Fiber stacks are removed. Dead-owner cleanup, exact current-owner comparison, and foreign-owner rejection remain in their original order.

leaveShared removes an owner only when it belongs to the captured current context, then removes the id only from that context. Container get, make and external lookup paths still enter before try and leave in finally after successful entry. Rejected entry cannot pop another context or clear its ownership.

Insertion order, repeated final id and strval conversion of numeric array keys are unchanged in both contexts. Existing numeric service contracts exercise shared/fresh resolution in main and Fiber contexts.

characterization_review.assessment: The two dataset variants exercise the actual overlapping local-cycle/foreign-owner state through Container::make/get and alias identities. They assert the circular chain, retain the suspended owner, reject concurrent shared access, then verify the eventual exact shared result and a bounded factory count. The third case checks main-context ownership rejecting a nested Fiber and later alias reuse. These are public behavior contracts, not implementation-shape assertions.
characterization_review.failure_bounding: Factories throw after an unexpected extra construction; the suspended owner is resumed in finally when necessary. The ownership-first mutant changes exactly the public precedence these two variants assert.
characterization_review.baseline_expected: These characterize existing successful behavior and must pass baseline as well as candidate; no baseline defect is claimed.

measurement_scope: Only repeated operations are timed; fixture setup, verification, warmup, garbage collection, Fiber construction/start/getReturn and JSON rendering are outside timers.

checks.raw_logs: stdout/stderr captured as bytes and saved without text normalization; byte counts and SHA-256 retained before exit/JSON/origin validation. Exceptions preserve appended records and failed status; no retry path exists.
checks.ordering: Nested runtime/round/position loops call blocking subprocess.run; each round is baseline, candidate, candidate, baseline. No overlapping children are launched by this driver.
checks.cwd_and_commands: Absolute binary/worker/source/autoloader arguments and selected source-tree cwd are recorded. Fixed reviewed worker uses absolute selected loader/vendor paths and has no timed cwd-dependent reads.
checks.elapsed_arithmetic: Every sample requires expected operation count, elapsed_ns > 0 and ns_per_operation == elapsed_ns / count. Counts differ only for build/default. Runtime series/binary/vendor/INI/OPcache/JIT metadata are checked.
checks.summary_math: Each variant median is computed over its per-process ns/operation samples. Ratio-of-medians is candidate / baseline minus one. Paired round comparisons use the mean of each two-sample variant group; faster-round count tests the sign of candidate minus baseline.
checks.source_proof: Whole src PHP file maps and path-delimited content fingerprints are captured before and after the campaign. Each worker must emit one successful source-origin proof for the selected src, six functions and at least 100 declarations.
checks.identity_readback: Before/after identities cover source loader, worker, driver, both binaries and four Composer metadata files. Loader hashes must be equal across source trees. Observed after-manifests are saved before equality validation, preserving failed readback evidence.
checks.failure_retention: No failed process is silently replaced or repeated. A new output directory is required; current run cannot overwrite previous measurement directories.

data.verdict: All recorded calculations and identity gates pass. A narrow predeclared repeat is warranted for the PHP84 transform/one directional slowdown and unstable build/default measurement.

specific_concerns.observation: All five paired changes are slower, with median paired +3.054054%; ratio of raw medians is +2.433532% (+414.1666 ns). Samples span roughly 164-210 ms, so this is not just a sub-millisecond timer-resolution issue. One narrow longer repeat is justified; five directional pairs from a shared-host multi-case campaign do not identify a causal code regression.
specific_concerns.source_path: The callable is an already valid static array, the input is explicit int, and the transform callback has only its semantic parameter. On this warmed path the changed AttributePlan::has is reached twice for the authoritative-provider miss. ParameterTarget::firstAttribute is not used by this built-in path, and no service resolution needs CycleGuard. No additional callback, autoload, or persistent state was introduced by the changed has scan.

specific_concerns.observation: Each main-campaign sample measures only 100 builds (roughly 8-20 ms). PHP84 has four slower pairs, including a +58.47% outlier; PHP85 ratio-of-medians -21.27% differs materially from median paired -11.79%. Neither overall percentage is a stable build-cost claim yet.
specific_concerns.source_path: The operation creates a complete fresh configured container in a loaded process. Default construction initializes the same core graph and built-in definitions; the final Config lookup traverses the changed main shared-entry guard, while the helper firstAttribute and parameter attribute selection are not the main workload. Container graphs are cyclic, and measure disables GC inside the loop. Increasing a single batch from100 to2000 changes retained-graph/memory pressure.

agreed_followup.reporting: Report both campaigns, absolute ns and both aggregation definitions. Do not replace or discard original samples, invent an acceptance threshold, or extrapolate to application latency.

inference.php84_transform_one: Main ratio-of-medians +2.433532% and five slower pairs became +0.136349% with three faster and four slower pairs. The prior consistent direction and magnitude did not persist. This does not prove exact equality or exclude small/context-dependent effects.
inference.php85_transform_one: Followup ratio-of-medians is -1.169878%, but only three of seven paired rounds are faster. The aggregate difference alone does not establish a repeatable improvement.
inference.build_default: Followup ratios are +0.301957% on PHP84 (four faster pairs) and -0.548953% on PHP85 (five faster pairs). The original large PHP85 -21.27% observation is not reproduced. All batches, including first batches, remain included; this is still a warmed-process construction workload.
inference.controls: Shared get is unchanged and serves as an observation of variation. Its results are not subtracted from other cases or treated as a calibration.
inference.comparison_boundary: Compare baseline versus candidate within each campaign. The followup filters preceding workloads and averages 20 separate 100-build batches rather than one 100-build sample, so absolute times across campaigns are not the same estimator or workload history.
inference.completion: The specific uncertainty received one predeclared larger repeat. No additional timing campaign or speculative code change is recommended from these observations alone.
